subproblems.title: Densities transfer under ball-mass scaling
subproblems.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, let μ, ν be measures on ℝ^N (Euclidean N), y, z ∈ ℝ^N, t > 0, δ > 0, c ∈ [0,∞] with c ≠ ∞, and θ ∈ [0,∞]. Suppose that for every ρ with 0 < ρ < δ, ν(B_ρ(y)) = c·(ofReal((t⁻¹)^n)·μ(B_{tρ}(z))) (closed balls, arithmetic in ℝ≥0∞), and that HasDensity n μ z θ, i.e. densityRatio n μ z ρ = μ(B_ρ(z))/(ω_n·ofReal(ρ)^n) → θ as ρ ↓ 0. Then HasDensity n ν y (c·θ).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (μ ν : Measure (Euclidean N)) (y z : Euclidean N) (t δ : ℝ) (c θ : ℝ≥0∞), 0 < t → 0 < δ → c ≠ ∞ → (∀ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ → ρ < δ → ν (closedBall y ρ) = c * (ENNReal.ofReal (t⁻¹ ^ n) * μ (closedBall z (t * ρ)))) → HasDensity n μ z θ → HasDensity n ν y (c * θ)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: extracted from steps 6 and 9 of the parent proof, where the identity densityRatio n μ_{W_j} y ρ = a⁻¹·densityRatio n μ_V (x + t_j•y) (t_j ρ) is combined with ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul. Here it is stated once for two arbitrary measures.

Notation: ω := unitBallVolume n = volume(ball(0,1) ⊆ EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)); densityRatio n m p ρ = m(closedBall p ρ)/(ω·ofReal(ρ)^n). All arithmetic is in [0,∞] = ℝ≥0∞, and a/b = b⁻¹·a (ENNReal.div_eq_inv_mul).

1. (ω is positive and finite.) The open unit ball of EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) is nonempty and open. volume is an additive Haar measure, so the ball has positive measure (Metric.measure_ball_pos with radius 1 > 0). The ball is bounded in a proper space, so its measure is finite (measure_ball_lt_top). Thus ω ≠ 0 and ω ≠ ∞.

2. (The radius map.) Let s(ρ) := tρ. s is continuous with s(0) = t·0 = 0, so s(ρ) → 0 as ρ → 0, hence also along 𝓝[>] 0 (nhdsWithin_le_nhds). For ρ > 0 we have s(ρ) = tρ > 0 since t > 0. By tendsto_nhdsWithin_iff, s tends to 𝓝[>] 0 along 𝓝[>] 0.

3. (Limit of the rescaled quotient.) Composing HasDensity n μ z θ, a limit along 𝓝[>] 0, with step 2 gives densityRatio n μ z (tρ) → θ as ρ → 0⁺. Since c ≠ ∞, ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul (side condition: θ ≠ 0 ∨ c ≠ ∞) gives c·densityRatio n μ z (tρ) → c·θ as ρ → 0⁺.

4. (Pointwise identity for 0 < ρ < δ.) Fix ρ ∈ (0,δ). Write M := μ(closedBall z (tρ)), T := ofReal(t)^n and P := ofReal(ρ)^n.
  - Since t > 0, ofReal((t⁻¹)^n) = ofReal(t⁻¹)^n = ((ofReal t)⁻¹)^n = T⁻¹ (ENNReal.ofReal_pow with t⁻¹ ≥ 0, ENNReal.ofReal_inv_of_pos, ENNReal.inv_pow).
  - ofReal(tρ)^n = (ofReal t·ofReal ρ)^n = T·P (ENNReal.ofReal_mul with t ≥ 0, mul_pow).
  - T ≠ 0 because ofReal t > 0, and T ≠ ∞.
  By hypothesis ν(closedBall y ρ) = c·(T⁻¹·M). Using (ω·P)⁻¹ = ω⁻¹·P⁻¹ (ENNReal.mul_inv, valid since ω ≠ 0 and ω ≠ ∞):
    densityRatio n ν y ρ = (ω·P)⁻¹·(c·(T⁻¹·M)) = ω⁻¹·P⁻¹·c·T⁻¹·M.
  Similarly, using ENNReal.mul_inv first with ω ∈ (0,∞) and then with T ∈ (0,∞):
    c·densityRatio n μ z (tρ) = c·((ω·(T·P))⁻¹·M) = c·(ω⁻¹·(T⁻¹·P⁻¹)·M).
  The two right-hand sides are equal by commutativity and associativity of multiplication in [0,∞]. Hence c·densityRatio n μ z (tρ) = densityRatio n ν y ρ for every ρ ∈ (0,δ).

5. (Conclusion.) Since δ > 0, the interval Ioo 0 δ belongs to 𝓝[>] 0 (Ioo_mem_nhdsGT). So by step 4 the functions ρ ↦ c·densityRatio n μ z (tρ) and ρ ↦ densityRatio n ν y ρ are eventually equal along 𝓝[>] 0. By step 3 and Tendsto.congr', densityRatio n ν y ρ → c·θ as ρ → 0⁺, which is HasDensity n ν y (c·θ). ∎
proof_key_steps: ω_n = unitBallVolume n lies in (0,∞) (measure_ball_pos, measure_ball_lt_top).
ρ ↦ tρ maps 𝓝[>]0 to 𝓝[>]0, so densityRatio n μ z (tρ) → θ; multiplying by c ≠ ∞ gives the limit c·θ (ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul).
For 0<ρ<δ: ofReal(t⁻¹^n) = (ofReal t^n)⁻¹ and ofReal(tρ)^n = ofReal t^n·ofReal ρ^n give densityRatio n ν y ρ = c·densityRatio n μ z (tρ) (ENNReal.mul_inv, ring).
Eventual equality on Ioo 0 δ ∈ 𝓝[>]0 and Tendsto.congr' yield HasDensity n ν y (c·θ).

subproblems.title: Masses of the rescaled varifold measure on cylinders and closed balls
subproblems.statement: Let V be an n-varifold on U ⊆ ℝ^N (V : Varifold N n U), x ∈ ℝ^N, t ∈ ℝ, and V_{x,t} := rescaledMeasure V x t = ofReal((t⁻¹)^n) • (φ_t)_# V.measure with φ_t(z,S) = (t⁻¹•(z − x), S). Then (i) for every Borel A ⊆ ℝ^N, V_{x,t}(A × G(N,n)) = ofReal((t⁻¹)^n)·μ_V({z : t⁻¹•(z − x) ∈ A}); and (ii) if t > 0, then for all y ∈ ℝ^N and ρ ∈ ℝ, V_{x,t}(B_ρ(y) × G(N,n)) = ofReal((t⁻¹)^n)·μ_V(B_{tρ}(x + t•y)), with closed balls.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclidean N)) (V : Varifold N n U) (x : Euclidean N) (t : ℝ), (∀ A : Set (Euclidean N), MeasurableSet A → rescaledMeasure V x t (A ×ˢ (univ : Set (Grassmannian N n))) = ENNReal.ofReal (t⁻¹ ^ n) * V.weight {z | t⁻¹ • (z - x) ∈ A}) ∧ (0 < t → ∀ (y : Euclidean N) (ρ : ℝ), rescaledMeasure V x t (closedBall y ρ ×ˢ (univ : Set (Grassmannian N n))) = ENNReal.ofReal (t⁻¹ ^ n) * V.weight (closedBall (x + t • y) (t * ρ)))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent proof.

1. (Measurability.) The map φ(z,S) := (t⁻¹•(z − x), S) on ℝ^N × G(N,n) is continuous, hence Borel measurable. By definition, rescaledMeasure V x t = ofReal((t⁻¹)^n) • V.measure.map φ.

2. (Part (i).) Let A ⊆ ℝ^N be Borel. Then A × G is Borel. The set A' := {z : t⁻¹•(z − x) ∈ A} is Borel, being the preimage of A under the continuous map z ↦ t⁻¹•(z − x).
  - Measure.smul_apply and Measure.map_apply (φ measurable, A × G measurable) give rescaledMeasure V x t (A × G) = ofReal((t⁻¹)^n)·V.measure(φ⁻¹(A × G)).
  - (z,S) ∈ φ⁻¹(A × G) iff t⁻¹•(z − x) ∈ A iff (z,S) ∈ A' × G, so φ⁻¹(A × G) = A' × G.
  - Varifold.weight_apply (A' Borel) gives V.measure(A' × G) = μ_V(A').
  Combining these proves (i).

3. (Part (ii).) Assume t > 0 and fix y ∈ ℝ^N, ρ ∈ ℝ. Apply (i) with A := closedBall y ρ, which is closed and hence Borel. It remains to show {w : t⁻¹•(w − x) ∈ closedBall y ρ} = closedBall (x + t•y) (tρ).
  - For w ∈ ℝ^N, t⁻¹•(w − (x + t•y)) = t⁻¹•w − t⁻¹•x − (t⁻¹t)•y = t⁻¹•(w − x) − y, because t⁻¹t = 1 (smul_sub, smul_add, smul_smul, inv_mul_cancel₀, one_smul).
  - Hence dist(t⁻¹•(w − x), y) = ‖t⁻¹•(w − (x + t•y))‖ = t⁻¹·‖w − (x + t•y)‖, since t⁻¹ > 0 (norm_smul, abs_of_pos).
  - As t > 0, t⁻¹·d ≤ ρ iff d ≤ tρ (div_le_iff₀).
  So w lies in the left-hand set iff dist(w, x + t•y) ≤ tρ, i.e. iff w ∈ closedBall (x + t•y) (tρ). Substituting this set identity into (i) gives (ii). ∎
proof_key_steps: rescaledMeasure V x t = ofReal(t⁻¹^n) • V.measure.map φ with φ(z,S) = (t⁻¹•(z−x),S) continuous.
φ⁻¹(A × G) = {z : t⁻¹•(z−x) ∈ A} × G; Measure.smul_apply, Measure.map_apply and Varifold.weight_apply give (i).
For t > 0: t⁻¹•(w−x) − y = t⁻¹•(w − (x+t•y)), so {w : t⁻¹•(w−x) ∈ B_ρ(y)} = B_{tρ}(x+t•y), and (ii) follows from (i).

subproblems.title: A scaled restriction of a locally finite measure to Ω × G is a varifold on Ω
subproblems.statement: Let Ω ⊆ ℝ^N be open, μ a measure on ℝ^N × G(N,n), and c ∈ [0,∞] with c ≠ ∞. Assume μ(K × G(N,n)) ≠ ∞ for every compact K ⊆ Ω. Then there is an n-varifold W on Ω (W : Varifold N n Ω) whose measure is W.measure = c • μ⌞(Ω × G(N,n)).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (Ω : Set (Euclidean N)) (μ : Measure (Euclidean N × Grassmannian N n)) (c : ℝ≥0∞), IsOpen Ω → c ≠ ∞ → (∀ K : Set (Euclidean N), IsCompact K → K ⊆ Ω → μ (K ×ˢ (univ : Set (Grassmannian N n))) ≠ ∞) → ∃ W : Varifold N n Ω, W.measure = c • μ.restrict (Ω ×ˢ (univ : Set (Grassmannian N n)))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the parent proof (the construction of W_j and C_Ω), stated for a general measure μ.

1. Put m := c • μ.restrict(Ω × G). A Varifold N n Ω consists of four fields: openness of Ω, a measure, the support condition m(Ωᶜ × G) = 0, and finiteness m(K × G) ≠ ∞ for every compact K ⊆ Ω. Openness of Ω is a hypothesis.

2. (Support condition.) Ω is open, so Ωᶜ × G is Borel. Since (Ωᶜ × G) ∩ (Ω × G) = ∅, Measure.restrict_apply gives μ.restrict(Ω × G)(Ωᶜ × G) = μ(∅) = 0. Hence m(Ωᶜ × G) = c·0 = 0 (Measure.smul_apply, smul_zero).

3. (Finiteness on compact sets.) Let K ⊆ Ω be compact. Then m(K × G) = c·μ.restrict(Ω × G)(K × G). Measure.restrict_apply_le, which holds for every set, gives μ.restrict(Ω × G)(K × G) ≤ μ(K × G), and μ(K × G) ≠ ∞ by hypothesis. Since c ≠ ∞, the product is finite (ENNReal.mul_ne_top), so m(K × G) ≠ ∞.

4. Hence W := ⟨Ω open, m, step 2, step 3⟩ is a Varifold N n Ω, and W.measure = m = c • μ.restrict(Ω × G) holds by definition (rfl). ∎
proof_key_steps: Take m := c • μ.restrict (Ω × G).
m(Ωᶜ × G) = c·μ(∅) = 0 by Measure.restrict_apply, since Ωᶜ × G is Borel.
For compact K ⊆ Ω: m(K × G) ≤ c·μ(K × G) < ∞ (restrict_apply_le, c ≠ ∞).
Package these as a Varifold N n Ω; its measure is m by rfl.

subproblems.title: First-variation control of a scaled restricted measure gives locally bounded first variation and a bound on ‖δW‖
subproblems.statement: Let Ω ⊆ ℝ^N, μ a measure on ℝ^N × G(N,n), W an n-varifold on Ω, and c, β ∈ [0,∞] with c ≠ ∞ and β ≠ ∞, such that W.measure = c • μ⌞(Ω × G(N,n)). Assume that for every C¹ field X : ℝ^N → ℝ^N with compact support, tsupport X ⊆ Ω and ‖X(y)‖ ≤ 1 for all y, we have ofReal|∫ div_S X(z) dμ(z,S)| ≤ β, where div_S X(z) = Varifold.tangentialDivergence X z S. Then W has locally bounded first variation, and variationMeasure W O ≤ c·β for every O with IsRelCompactOpenIn O Ω.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (Ω : Set (Euclidean N)) (μ : Measure (Euclidean N × Grassmannian N n)) (W : Varifold N n Ω) (c β : ℝ≥0∞), c ≠ ∞ → β ≠ ∞ → W.measure = c • μ.restrict (Ω ×ˢ (univ : Set (Grassmannian N n))) → (∀ X : Euclidean N → Euclidean N, ContDiff ℝ 1 X → HasCompactSupport X → tsupport X ⊆ Ω → (∀ y, ‖X y‖ ≤ 1) → ENNReal.ofReal |∫ z, Varifold.tangentialDivergence X z.1 z.2 ∂μ| ≤ β) → W.HasLocallyBoundedFirstVariation ∧ ∀ O : Set (Euclidean N), IsRelCompactOpenIn O Ω → variationMeasure W O ≤ c * β
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the parent proof. That step proves the identity δW_j(X) = τ⁻¹∫div_S X dV_j and passes from a bound on |δW_j(X)| to firstVariationNormOn, LBFV and variationMeasure. Here the rescaled-divergence estimate is abstracted as the hypothesis.

Notation: δW(X) = W.firstVariation X = ∫ div_S X(z) dW.measure(z,S).

1. (First-variation identity.) Let X ∈ Varifold.TestVectorField Ω: C¹, compact support, tsupport X ⊆ Ω. We claim δW(X) = c.toReal·∫ div_S X dμ.
  - By W.measure = c • μ.restrict(Ω × G) and integral_smul_measure (∫ f d(c•m) = c.toReal • ∫ f dm, for every f and c), δW(X) = c.toReal·∫_{Ω×G} div_S X dμ.
  - Let (z,S) ∉ Ω × G. Then z ∉ Ω, so z ∉ tsupport X. By Varifold.support_tangentialDivergence_subset, the support of (z,S) ↦ div_S X(z) lies in tsupport X × G, so div_S X(z) = 0.
  - Hence ∫_{Ω×G} div_S X dμ = ∫ div_S X dμ (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero), proving the claim.

2. (Uniform bound.) For every set O ⊆ ℝ^N, W.firstVariationNormOn O ≤ c·β. By definition, firstVariationNormOn O is the supremum over X ∈ TestVectorField Ω of: ofReal|δW(X)| if X.UnitSupportedIn O (tsupport X ⊆ O and ‖X(y)‖ ≤ 1 for all y), and 0 otherwise. By iSup_le it suffices to bound each term.
  - The term 0 is ≤ c·β.
  - If X is unit-supported in O: by step 1 and c.toReal ≥ 0, |δW(X)| = c.toReal·|∫ div_S X dμ| (abs_mul, abs_of_nonneg). Hence ofReal|δW(X)| = ofReal(c.toReal)·ofReal|∫ div_S X dμ| = c·ofReal|∫ div_S X dμ| (ENNReal.ofReal_mul; ENNReal.ofReal_toReal, using c ≠ ∞).
  - This is ≤ c·β by the hypothesis applied to X: X is C¹ with compact support, tsupport X ⊆ Ω because X is a test field on Ω, and ‖X(y)‖ ≤ 1 for all y.

3. (Locally bounded first variation.) c·β ≠ ∞ because c ≠ ∞ and β ≠ ∞ (ENNReal.mul_ne_top). By step 2, for every open O with compact closure contained in Ω, W.firstVariationNormOn O ≤ c·β < ∞. This is W.HasLocallyBoundedFirstVariation (call it hLBFV).

4. (Bound for ‖δW‖.) Let IsRelCompactOpenIn O Ω: O open, closure O compact, closure O ⊆ Ω.
  - By definition of variationMeasure, and since W has LBFV (positive branch of the dite, dif_pos), variationMeasure W = W.firstVariationRieszMeasure hLBFV.
  - SimonGMT Varifold.firstVariationRieszMeasure_eq_norm, applicable because O is open with compact closure ⊆ Ω, gives W.firstVariationRieszMeasure hLBFV O = W.firstVariationNormOn O.
  - By step 2 this is ≤ c·β, so variationMeasure W O ≤ c·β. ∎
proof_key_steps: For test fields X on Ω, δW(X) = c.toReal·∫ div_S X dμ (integral_smul_measure; the integrand vanishes off Ω × G by support_tangentialDivergence_subset).
Hence ofReal|δW(X)| = c·ofReal|∫ div_S X dμ| ≤ c·β for unit fields, so firstVariationNormOn O ≤ c·β for every O (iSup_le).
c·β < ∞ gives W.HasLocallyBoundedFirstVariation.
variationMeasure W = firstVariationRieszMeasure (dif_pos), and firstVariationRieszMeasure_eq_norm gives variationMeasure W O ≤ c·β when IsRelCompactOpenIn O Ω.

subproblems.title: Mass bound for rescaled bad sets in the restricted blow-up
subproblems.statement: Let V be an n-varifold on U ⊆ ℝ^N, x ∈ ℝ^N, t > 0, R > 0, and c ∈ [0,∞]. Let W be an n-varifold on the open ball B°_R(0) with W.measure = c • (rescaledMeasure V x t)⌞(B°_R(0) × G(N,n)), and let E, O ⊆ ℝ^N be arbitrary sets with O ⊆ B°_R(0). Then μ_W({y : x + t•y ∈ E} ∩ O) ≤ c·(ofReal(R)^n·(μ_V({z : z ∈ B_{tR}(x) ∧ z ∈ E}) / ofReal(tR)^n)), where B_{tR}(x) is the closed ball and the measures are applied to arbitrary sets as outer measures.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclidean N)) (V : Varifold N n U) (x : Euclidean N) (t R : ℝ) (c : ℝ≥0∞) (W : Varifold N n (ball (0 : Euclidean N) R)) (E O : Set (Euclidean N)), 0 < t → 0 < R → W.measure = c • (rescaledMeasure V x t).restrict (ball (0 : Euclidean N) R ×ˢ (univ : Set (Grassmannian N n))) → O ⊆ ball (0 : Euclidean N) R → W.weight ({y | x + t • y ∈ E} ∩ O) ≤ c * (ENNReal.ofReal R ^ n * (V.weight {z | z ∈ closedBall x (t * R) ∧ z ∈ E} / ENNReal.ofReal (t * R) ^ n))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 7 of the parent proof, for one fixed scale t. The parent applies it with t = t_j, c = (ofReal τ)⁻¹, and E the set where Θ^n(μ_V,·) ≥ τ fails. No hypothesis on c is needed: every step below is monotone in c.

1. (Measurable hull.) Put E' := {z : z ∈ closedBall x (tR) ∧ z ∈ E} and Ẽ := toMeasurable μ_V E'. Then Ẽ is Borel (measurableSet_toMeasurable), E' ⊆ Ẽ (subset_toMeasurable), and μ_V(Ẽ) = μ_V(E') (measure_toMeasurable). Let A := {y : x + t•y ∈ Ẽ}. A is Borel as the preimage of Ẽ under the continuous map y ↦ x + t•y.

2. (Inclusion.) We show {y : x + t•y ∈ E} ∩ O ⊆ A. Let x + t•y ∈ E and y ∈ O. Since O ⊆ ball 0 R, ‖y‖ < R. So dist(x + t•y, x) = ‖t•y‖ = t‖y‖ ≤ tR, using t > 0 (add_sub_cancel_left, norm_smul, abs_of_pos). Hence x + t•y ∈ E' ⊆ Ẽ, i.e. y ∈ A.

3. (Pass to the rescaled measure.) By step 2 and monotonicity of measures:
  μ_W({y : x + t•y ∈ E} ∩ O) ≤ μ_W(A) = W.measure(A × G)   (Varifold.weight_apply, A Borel)
    = c·(rescaledMeasure V x t).restrict(ball 0 R × G)(A × G)   (Measure.smul_apply)
    ≤ c·rescaledMeasure V x t (A × G).
  The last inequality holds because restriction does not increase a measure (Measure.restrict_le_self) and multiplication by c is monotone.

4. (Rescaled mass.) By part (i) of the sibling rescaled_mass_formula (Submission.varifold_tangents_dlb_rescaledMeasure_prod_univ, applied to the Borel set A), rescaledMeasure V x t (A × G) = ofReal((t⁻¹)^n)·μ_V({z : t⁻¹•(z − x) ∈ A}).
  - For every z, x + t•(t⁻¹•(z − x)) = x + (z − x) = z, since t ≠ 0 (smul_smul, mul_inv_cancel₀, one_smul, add_sub_cancel).
  - So {z : t⁻¹•(z − x) ∈ A} = {z : z ∈ Ẽ} = Ẽ, and μ_V(Ẽ) = μ_V(E') by step 1.
  Thus rescaledMeasure V x t (A × G) = ofReal((t⁻¹)^n)·μ_V(E').

5. (Arithmetic.) Let T := ofReal(t)^n and Q := ofReal(R)^n; both lie in (0,∞) because t, R > 0. Write M := μ_V(E').
  - ofReal((t⁻¹)^n) = T⁻¹ (ENNReal.ofReal_pow, ENNReal.ofReal_inv_of_pos, ENNReal.inv_pow).
  - ofReal(tR)^n = T·Q (ENNReal.ofReal_mul, mul_pow).
  - Q·(M/(T·Q)) = Q·((T·Q)⁻¹·M) = Q·(T⁻¹·Q⁻¹)·M (ENNReal.mul_inv, using T ∈ (0,∞)) = (Q·Q⁻¹)·(T⁻¹·M) = T⁻¹·M (ENNReal.mul_inv_cancel, Q ≠ 0, Q ≠ ∞).
  Hence ofReal((t⁻¹)^n)·μ_V(E') = ofReal(R)^n·(μ_V(E')/ofReal(tR)^n).

6. (Conclusion.) Steps 3–5 give μ_W({y : x + t•y ∈ E} ∩ O) ≤ c·(ofReal(R)^n·(μ_V(E')/ofReal(tR)^n)), where E' = {z : z ∈ closedBall x (tR) ∧ z ∈ E}. This is the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: Replace E' = {z ∈ closedBall x (tR) : z ∈ E} by its measurable hull Ẽ = toMeasurable μ_V E', and set A = {y : x + t•y ∈ Ẽ} (Borel).
{y : x+t•y ∈ E} ∩ O ⊆ A, because ‖y‖ < R puts x + t•y in closedBall x (tR).
μ_W(A) = W.measure(A × G) ≤ c·rescaledMeasure V x t (A × G) (Measure.restrict_le_self).
Sibling rescaled_mass_formula (i) and {z : t⁻¹•(z−x) ∈ A} = Ẽ give c·ofReal(t⁻¹^n)·μ_V(E').
ENNReal arithmetic: ofReal(t⁻¹^n)·M = ofReal(R)^n·(M/ofReal(tR)^n).

subproblems.title: Densities of the restricted blow-up at points whose image has a density
subproblems.statement: Let V be an n-varifold on U ⊆ ℝ^N, x ∈ ℝ^N, t > 0, R ∈ ℝ, c ∈ [0,∞] with c ≠ ∞, and θ ∈ [0,∞]. Let W be an n-varifold on the open ball B°_R(0) with W.measure = c • (rescaledMeasure V x t)⌞(B°_R(0) × G(N,n)), and let y ∈ B°_R(0) satisfy HasDensity n μ_V (x + t•y) θ. Then HasDensity n μ_W y (c·θ).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclidean N)) (V : Varifold N n U) (x : Euclidean N) (t R : ℝ) (c θ : ℝ≥0∞) (W : Varifold N n (ball (0 : Euclidean N) R)) (y : Euclidean N), 0 < t → c ≠ ∞ → W.measure = c • (rescaledMeasure V x t).restrict (ball (0 : Euclidean N) R ×ˢ (univ : Set (Grassmannian N n))) → y ∈ ball (0 : Euclidean N) R → HasDensity n V.weight (x + t • y) θ → HasDensity n W.weight y (c * θ)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 6 of the parent proof, for one fixed scale t. The parent applies it with t = t_j and c = (ofReal τ)⁻¹, at points y ∈ Ω with x + t_j•y ∉ E.

1. Since y ∈ ball 0 R, ‖y‖ < R (mem_ball_zero_iff). Put δ := R − ‖y‖ > 0.

2. (Small balls stay in the domain.) For 0 < ρ < δ, closedBall y ρ ⊆ ball 0 R. Indeed, if ‖w − y‖ ≤ ρ then ‖w‖ ≤ ‖w − y‖ + ‖y‖ ≤ ρ + ‖y‖ < R (norm_add_le applied to w = (w − y) + y).

3. (Ball masses.) For 0 < ρ < δ:
  μ_W(closedBall y ρ) = W.measure(closedBall y ρ × G)   (Varifold.weight_apply; closed balls are Borel)
    = c·rescaledMeasure V x t((closedBall y ρ × G) ∩ (ball 0 R × G))   (Measure.smul_apply; Measure.restrict_apply, since closedBall y ρ × G is Borel)
    = c·rescaledMeasure V x t(closedBall y ρ × G)   (by step 2 the intersection is closedBall y ρ × G: inter_eq_left, prod_mono)
    = c·(ofReal((t⁻¹)^n)·μ_V(closedBall (x + t•y) (tρ))).
  The last equality is part (ii) of the sibling rescaled_mass_formula (Submission.varifold_tangents_dlb_rescaledMeasure_prod_univ), using t > 0.

4. (Apply the scaling lemma.) Apply the sibling density_scaling (Submission.varifold_tangents_dlb_hasDensity_of_closedBall_scaling) with (μ, ν, y, z, t, δ, c, θ) := (μ_V, μ_W, y, x + t•y, t, δ, c, θ). Its hypotheses are:
  - t > 0, δ > 0 and c ≠ ∞;
  - the identity of step 3 for every ρ ∈ (0,δ);
  - HasDensity n μ_V (x + t•y) θ.
  Its conclusion is HasDensity n μ_W y (c·θ). ∎
proof_key_steps: δ := R − ‖y‖ > 0, and closedBall y ρ ⊆ ball 0 R for 0 < ρ < δ.
μ_W(B_ρ(y)) = c·rescaledMeasure V x t (B_ρ(y) × G) = c·(ofReal(t⁻¹^n)·μ_V(B_{tρ}(x+t•y))) (Measure.restrict_apply; sibling rescaled_mass_formula (ii)).
Sibling density_scaling with z = x + t•y gives HasDensity n μ_W y (c·θ).

subproblems.title: Density lower bounds pull back from a scaled restriction to the original varifold
subproblems.statement: Let V be an n-varifold on U ⊆ ℝ^N and W an n-varifold on Ω ⊆ ℝ^N (so Ω is open). Let c ∈ [0,∞] with c ≠ 0 and c ≠ ∞, and suppose W.measure = c • V.measure⌞(Ω × G(N,n)). Suppose also that for μ_W-a.e. y there is θ with HasDensity n μ_W y θ and 1 ≤ θ. Then for μ_V-a.e. y: if y ∈ Ω, there is θ with HasDensity n μ_V y θ and c⁻¹ ≤ θ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (U Ω : Set (Euclidean N)) (V : Varifold N n U) (W : Varifold N n Ω) (c : ℝ≥0∞), c ≠ 0 → c ≠ ∞ → W.measure = c • V.measure.restrict (Ω ×ˢ (univ : Set (Grassmannian N n))) → (∀ᵐ y ∂W.weight, ∃ θ : ℝ≥0∞, HasDensity n W.weight y θ ∧ 1 ≤ θ) → ∀ᵐ y ∂V.weight, y ∈ Ω → ∃ θ : ℝ≥0∞, HasDensity n V.weight y θ ∧ c⁻¹ ≤ θ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 9 of the parent proof (the transfer from C_Ω back to C), stated for an arbitrary varifold V. The parent applies it with V = C, W = C_Ω and c = (ofReal τ)⁻¹, so that c⁻¹ = ofReal τ (inv_inv).

1. Ω is open (W.isOpen_domain), hence Borel.

2. (Weight identity.) We show μ_W = c • (μ_V⌞Ω). For Borel A:
  μ_W(A) = W.measure(A × G)   (Varifold.weight_apply)
    = c·V.measure((A × G) ∩ (Ω × G))   (Measure.smul_apply; Measure.restrict_apply, A × G Borel)
    = c·V.measure((A ∩ Ω) × G)   (prod_inter_prod, inter_univ)
    = c·μ_V(A ∩ Ω)   (Varifold.weight_apply, A ∩ Ω Borel)
    = c·(μ_V⌞Ω)(A)   (Measure.restrict_apply).
  Measures that agree on all Borel sets are equal (Measure.ext).

3. (Null sets.) Since c ≠ 0, μ_V⌞Ω ≪ c • (μ_V⌞Ω) = μ_W (Measure.absolutelyContinuous_smul). So the hypothesis 'for μ_W-a.e. y, ∃θ, HasDensity n μ_W y θ ∧ 1 ≤ θ' also holds μ_V⌞Ω-a.e. (AbsolutelyContinuous.ae_le). Since Ω is Borel, ae_restrict_iff' turns this into: for μ_V-a.e. y, y ∈ Ω ⇒ ∃θ, HasDensity n μ_W y θ ∧ 1 ≤ θ.

4. (Ball masses near a good point.) Fix such a y ∈ Ω and its θ. Since Ω is open, there is δ > 0 with ball y δ ⊆ Ω (Metric.isOpen_iff). For 0 < ρ < δ, closedBall y ρ ⊆ ball y δ ⊆ Ω (closedBall_subset_ball). So by step 2, μ_W(closedBall y ρ) = c·μ_V(closedBall y ρ ∩ Ω) = c·μ_V(closedBall y ρ). As 0 < c < ∞, c⁻¹·c = 1 (ENNReal.inv_mul_cancel), hence
  μ_V(closedBall y ρ) = c⁻¹·μ_W(closedBall y ρ) = c⁻¹·(ofReal((1⁻¹)^n)·μ_W(closedBall y (1·ρ))),
  using ofReal((1⁻¹)^n) = ofReal 1 = 1 and 1·ρ = ρ.

5. (Apply the scaling lemma.) Apply the sibling density_scaling (Submission.varifold_tangents_dlb_hasDensity_of_closedBall_scaling) with (μ, ν, y, z, t, δ, c, θ) := (μ_W, μ_V, y, y, 1, δ, c⁻¹, θ). Its hypotheses are:
  - 1 > 0 and δ > 0;
  - c⁻¹ ≠ ∞, because c ≠ 0 (ENNReal.inv_ne_top);
  - the identity of step 4 for every ρ ∈ (0,δ);
  - HasDensity n μ_W y θ.
  It gives HasDensity n μ_V y (c⁻¹·θ). Finally c⁻¹ = c⁻¹·1 ≤ c⁻¹·θ because 1 ≤ θ. So θ' := c⁻¹·θ witnesses the claim at y, and by step 3 this holds for μ_V-a.e. y ∈ Ω. ∎
proof_key_steps: Ω is open (the domain of W), hence Borel.
μ_W = c • (μ_V⌞Ω), by evaluating both on Borel sets.
μ_V⌞Ω ≪ μ_W (c ≠ 0) and ae_restrict_iff' give: for μ_V-a.e. y ∈ Ω, W has a density θ ≥ 1 at y.
For such y, closedBall y ρ ⊆ Ω for small ρ, so μ_V(B_ρ(y)) = c⁻¹·μ_W(B_ρ(y)).
Sibling density_scaling with t = 1 and constant c⁻¹ gives HasDensity n μ_V y (c⁻¹θ), and c⁻¹θ ≥ c⁻¹.
